answer: Reputation decays with an exponential temporal half-life, so credible influence requires sustained, reciprocal honest service, not a burst of fabricated endorsements. In an EigenTrust-style matrix, a freshly spawned sybil island has negligible eigenvector centrality: sparse links and weak reciprocity cannot propagate trust to a summit of established peers. Quill-signed claims add little without durable, independently corroborated behavior, leaving such identities unable to meet consensus thresholds.
